sections.content:
# Isolate JVM effects and qualify the complete Shx portable surface

## Outcome

Isolate JVM effects and qualify the complete Shx portable surface. The observable contracts below are fulfilled on every required host after qualification.

## Context

These are initial Incoming Markdown planning inputs. Their parent reference is the unchanged existing eight-point `shx-kanban-port-shx-to-cljc` card. That card is still Todo, category tasks, with no accepted epic/type conversion. Review must decide whether to promote its role through Rheos and admit this 3 + 3 + 2 decomposition, or revise the decomposition lawfully. The references propose a hierarchy; they do not demonstrate an operational transition, approved size or implementation permission. No duplicate umbrella is created. All three outcomes are required for the whole original card; a partial portable quote/schema patch cannot close it.

Current owning source is `f4ee133dcf1650c7eafb623ef084f62417252477`; personal sync PR1 is the pending stack base. The original card’s Clio precedent is a routing claim, not permission to copy a child’s code or assert common-law promotion.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] JVM filesystem, EDN reading, environment/home lookup, hostname process, warning/exit and subprocess effects from infra/config, infra/fs and cli are isolated behind an explicitly reviewed Shx extern adapter contract, retaining compatibility facades and actual command behavior.
- [ ] Preserve mandatory top-level config failure exit, warning/degrading fragments, canonical cycle detection and existing include resolution, directory filtering/dedup/order and CLI render/check/emit/validate/invalid-target outcomes. Controlled private temp/child-process fixtures retain parent environment and two-run isolation. No login shell, global home config or live consumer is used as a fixture.
- [ ] The pure render decisions may move out of cli only after separating supplied environment/directory/hostname facts from effects; envm render-time collapsed PATH remains distinct from IR runtime per-entry guards.
- [ ] Actual JVM/NBB/compiled consumer fixtures cover all six current portable namespaces, generated output payload parity, meaningful negative and deliberate test-failure exit controls, and the retained full seven-check gate. Mutation discovery explicitly covers migrated `.cljc` executable logic and reports real survivors plus literal-schema attribution limits.
- [ ] Provide a reviewed real consumer import smoke on an isolated pinned fixture for each required host, full source/ABI comparison and a human verification script for JVM CLI behavior. Missing consumer/library/runner support or absent qualified predecessor code remains a hold, not green proof.

## Verification

Follow the complete red/green and discovery matrix in [the design](../docs/design/shx-portability-planning.md). Existing command `bin/analyze --strict` retains all seven checks. Future NBB/compiled runner commands, exact dependency closure and namespace discovery must be committed and reviewed before red; a guessed alias, zero-test pass or JVM-only suite is insufficient. Actual exit status and test/assertion counts are required.

## Scope

Existing `src/shx/infra/{config,fs}.clj`, `src/shx/cli.clj` compatibility/effect boundaries and complete host/CLI gate wiring.

## Out of scope

No supervisor IR additions, Clio/eta-mu source port, envm PATH redesign, implemented shx.core, Bash parser, namespace rename campaign, board engine or service deployment. PR2 tests, PR3 runtime and PR4 structural checking retain their separate full outcomes.

## Risks and review decisions

Whole original size remains eight points; proposed children sum to eight. Review the host dependency support, typed annotation strategy, adapter ABI, coverage discovery, mutation policy and overlap serialization before any lawful Ready transition. New host load is not runtime shx.core qualification, and historical baseline success is not this port’s green result.
